how.text: How to read this. Top row is the proposal as screens, plus the Screens sheet at the far right; middle row is the three new controls at full size; third row is the evidence, the model and the extras; the fourth row is how it folds on phones and tablets. Everything is dark-only and in the busk view's own vocabulary on purpose — these are the intended pixels, not structure to copy.

q1.text: Open call 1 — the rig's home. Drawn as one rig per project (one selection surface for every screen). The alternative, a rig per page, is declined on the Ideas board; say so if the colour page really should show fewer targets than the position page.

q2.text: Open call 2 — where Spread resolves. Drawn as POST /programmer/spread on the desk (group order, ranges, cells, emitters all live there). The cheap alternative is the client's fanMath over fixtures only, no groups and no cells — fine for a first cut, wrong the day a group is selected.

q3.text: Open call 3 — cells before the backend can press them. Drawn as: pips draw and the chip narrows from session 1, and a press on a cell target is refused by name until the element arm lands. The alternative is to hide the pips until session 5, which loses the live-per-cell feedback that costs nothing.

q4.text: Open call 4 — the split's unit. Drawn as whole rows (snap), because a half row of tiles is useless. If the band should instead be a free percentage, the handle is the same and only the clamp changes.

q5.text: Open call 5 — page on the Screens row. Drawn as settable (a remote set unlinks that window onto the page, as ?page= does). If that feels like reaching into another operator's window, make it read-only on the row and keep focus and sheet settable; the command shape does not change.
